Checked byte-buffer functions
=============================

checked-c/1 is a sequential, typed byte-buffer fragment. It compiles through
cesta cc and cesta build, and export-c writes ordinary C. Plain C continues
to use the native compiler directly.

    cesta checked check checked/examples/ByteViews.cesta
    cesta checked plan checked/examples/ByteViews.cesta -o permissions.plan
    cesta checked header checked/examples/ByteViews.cesta -o byte_views.h
    cesta export-c checked/examples/ByteViews.cesta -o byte_views.c --
    cesta cc -c checked/examples/ByteViews.cesta

A module names its C namespace and failure hook. A module using allocated
owners also names an allocator and release pair. word-bits is 32 or 64 and
defaults to 64; the generated C checks it against the target's size_t.

    (cesta checked-c/1
      (module example)
      (word-bits 64)
      (failure example_failure)
      (allocator example_allocate example_release)
      (fn sum
        (params (bytes read))
        (returns u64)
        (effects)
        (body
          (var total u64 (u64 0))
          (for index bytes
            (body (set total (wrap-add total (as u64 (at bytes index))))))
          (return total))))

Compiler hints
--------------

Build a checked module with -DCESTA_CHECKED_OPTIMIZE=1 to enable the compiler
hint layer, or pass --checked-hints to cesta build. The project option applies
the mode to every target source, participates in incremental command changes,
and is preserved in the exported Makefile. Without it the default is zero.
The ordinary C export retains the hints. The switch must be
set before including a generated checked header. Other values are rejected.
GCC and Clang receive cold/noinline on the generated failure wrapper and
alloc_size(1) on the declared byte allocator. Other C compilers receive the
same ordinary declarations without these attributes.

The failure wrapper calls the declared failure hook and never returns even
if that hook returns. The allocator must supply the requested byte extent on
success; it may return null. These hints do not add a nonnull, malloc,
restrict, pure, const or alignment promise. A short exclusive borrow does not
establish the whole-function precondition of restrict. Failure checks remain
observable and are retained in both modes.

test-checked-hints compares authored and exported builds in both modes under
GCC and Clang, runs the existing ownership and trap controls with sanitizers,
and independently checks the compiler's object-size knowledge. Hint emission
does not imply a speedup on every programme.

Types and interfaces
--------------------

unit is the result of a procedure. bool, u8, u16, u32, u64 and usize are
scalar types. read and write are borrowed byte views; own is an allocated
byte buffer transferred by value. Fixed local arrays have their own internal
owner kind and cannot escape as own or as a borrowed result.

The exported C interface uses cesta_read_bytes, cesta_write_bytes and
cesta_owned_bytes, each a pointer and size_t length. read has a const pointer.
There is no run-time borrow ledger. The compiler checks permissions before
emitting C; bounds, size, arithmetic and explicit require checks remain in C.

Every function declares params, returns, effects and body. A borrowed result
names its lifetime source: (returns read from bytes) or (returns write from
bytes). That source must be a compatible borrowed parameter. An owned result
transfers one allocated buffer; unreturned owners are released automatically.
The heap effect is required for allocating or releasing owned buffers.
Calling a function requires all its declared effects in the caller.
Effects name additional operations such as allocation or I/O; argument modes
separately describe access to supplied buffers. An empty effects list does
not assert referential transparency for a function with writable arguments.

    (import "FormatBytes.cesta" as Format)
    (let length usize (call Format_unsigned_decimal output value))

Imports resolve relative to the importing source and use an explicit local
prefix. Only the imported module's defined functions are exposed; its imports
and foreign declarations are not implicitly re-exported. Imported bodies are
checked recursively. Cycles, duplicate prefixes, direct C declaration
collisions and different word widths are refused. Calls pass the same
descriptor ABI used by defined functions.
An owned argument or result requires identical allocator/release names in
both modules. Borrowed-only calls do not require a common allocator family.
An import checks an interface; the project manifest still lists the source
units that supply its definitions. Compiler dependency files track every
transitive import, so a changed interface rechecks its callers.

Foreign code is declared explicitly:

    (foreign send native_send
      (params (bytes read)) (returns usize) (effects io)
      (obligation "Reads only the supplied initialized range; retains no pointer."))

A foreign read/write argument lowers to pointer,length native parameters.
Checked-to-checked calls use descriptor parameters instead.
Foreign own arguments and borrowed/owned results use descriptors. Foreign
implementations must satisfy their signature, lifetime and effect promises;
the obligation text does not prove them. A public function called from C has
the same obligations:
all ranges are valid and initialized, exclusive or consumed arguments do not
alias other arguments, and owners belong to this module's allocator pair.
An owned result is initialized and exclusive. A borrowed result lies in the
initialized range of its declared source and retains no longer lifetime.

Statements
----------

let and var declare initialized scalars; set changes a var. let may also bind
a borrowed call result or move/bind an owned result.

    (array bytes 8)                    zero-initialized local bytes
    (borrow view read bytes)           shared view; write requests exclusivity
    (slice view read bytes start size) checked subrange, same root lifetime
    (copy second view)                 scalar or read-view copy
    (move moved bytes)                 transfer; old binding becomes unusable
    (end view)                        end a borrow with no live reborrows
    (drop bytes)                      release an unborrowed owner
    (put view index (u8 7))            checked byte store
    (require condition)               always checked, including NDEBUG builds
    (call function arguments...)      checked signature and argument permissions
    (return value)                    evaluate result, then clean up, then return

    (if condition (then statements...) (else statements...))
    (while condition (body statements...))
    (for index view (body statements...))
    (break)
    (continue)
    (block statements...)
    (allocate bytes count (then statements...) (else statements...))

Allocation failure takes else. A zero-sized allocation succeeds without
calling the allocator. A successful allocation is initialized to zero before
its body. Buffers larger than PTRDIFF_MAX take the failure branch.

Block exits automatically end views and release remaining owners in reverse
declaration order, including return, break and continue. The failure hook is
fatal: if it returns, generated code spins. It is not an exception/unwinding
mechanism. All normal branch exits must agree on outer permissions. Loop
backedges and loop exits must restore the outer entry permissions.

A reborrow suspends conflicting access through its parent. Ending that
parent or moving its owner while a child is live is refused. Permissions
are conservative for an entire buffer: two disjoint write slices still
conflict. Pointer forging and arbitrary native expressions are unavailable
inside a checked body.

Expressions
-----------

Typed unsigned decimal literals use (u8 7), (u64 7) or (usize 7). bool uses
true and false. Available operations are len, at, not, and, or, eq, ne, lt,
le, gt, ge, add, sub, mul, div, rem, wrap-add, wrap-sub, wrap-mul, bit-and,
bit-or, bit-xor, shl and shr. Binary arithmetic operands have the same type;
shift counts are usize. add/sub/mul check overflow; div/rem reject zero;
shifts reject counts at or above the operand's width. wrap operations are
explicit modular arithmetic. as permits widening; truncate names narrowing.
Calls bind a let or return directly; nested calls in scalar expressions are
not supported.

Proof and testing boundary
-------------------------

The emitted cesta-permissions/1 plan is a projection of root permissions,
transfers, borrowed-result origins and structured control flow. Scalar work,
condition values and iteration counts are erased; it is not an exact effect
or cost trace. Short-circuit expressions are conservatively checked on both
sides. The independent Lean checker validates every branch, loop invariant,
call permission and return cleanup. Its laws cover all finite executions of
that permission model, including arbitrarily many loop iterations. Signatures
record their allocator/release family. Owned calls preserve that family;
borrowed returns preserve their source lifetime. An interface extension that
preserves already-resolved signatures preserves admitted plans.

Import plans appear before the importing module's record. export-c --plan
records the same projections while producing the actual C artifact. Repeated
imports may repeat a record. Interface laws do not establish which native
object a linker binds to a public name; supplied objects must implement their
recorded definitions.

Native allocator validity, foreign implementations, the source-to-plan
projection, scalar lowering, printed C and GCC/Clang compilation are outside
those permission proofs. Native runs, sanitizer controls and refused source
examples test the implementation boundaries. This fragment does not yet
provide general Rust ownership for records, enums, owned globals, threads,
arbitrary pointers or shared graphs.

make test-checked-core runs native and authored GCC/Clang controls.
make test-checked-libraries checks byte packing and numeric formatting.
make test-checked-imports checks calls, ownership and incremental builds across modules.
make test-checked-sanitizers adds ASan/UBSan.
make test-checked-model checks the laws and their proof dependencies.
make test-checked-admission admits actual emitted plans and refuses mutations.
make test-checked-generated additionally checks generated combinations of
scopes, calls, moves and loans, with native allocation accounting and sanitizers.
The core and library gates are in check; imports are in test. Model,
admission, generated-program and sanitizer gates are in qualify.
